title: Subsequent Events - ASC 855
learning_objectives: Distinguish Type I from Type II subsequent events

content.definition: Events or transactions that occur after balance sheet date but before financial statements issued or available to be issued

evaluation_period.public_companies: Through date financial statements are issued (filed with SEC)
evaluation_period.private_companies: Through date financial statements are available to be issued (given to users)

type_I_recognized.description: Events that provide additional evidence about conditions that existed AT balance sheet date
examples: Settlement of litigation if lawsuit existed at balance sheet date
Bankruptcy of customer with receivable outstanding at balance sheet date (adjust bad debt)
Sale of inventory below cost confirms inventory impairment that existed at year-end
Determination of purchase price allocation for acquisition at year-end
type_I_recognized.rationale: Conditions existed at balance sheet date; subsequent event provides evidence

type_II_nonrecognized.description: Events that provide evidence about conditions that DID NOT exist at balance sheet date
type_II_nonrecognized.accounting: DO NOT recognize - DISCLOSE if material
examples: Sale of bonds or stock after year-end
Loss on receivables from sales made after year-end
type_II_nonrecognized.disclosure: Nature of event and estimate of financial effect (or statement that estimate cannot be made)

decision_framework.question: Did condition exist at balance sheet date?

settlement_of_lawsuit.scenario: Lawsuit pending at 12/31, settled 1/15 for $500K. Financial statements issued 2/1.
settlement_of_lawsuit.treatment: Type I - Recognize. Adjust contingent liability to $500K.

fire_destroys_inventory.scenario: Inventory on hand at 12/31, fire destroys it on 1/10.
fire_destroys_inventory.treatment: Type II - Disclose only. Do not write down inventory in prior year statements.

customer_bankruptcy.scenario: Receivable from customer at 12/31. Customer declares bankruptcy 1/5.
customer_bankruptcy.treatment: Type I - Recognize. Increase allowance for doubtful accounts.

issue_stock_offering.condition_at_year_end: No - stock not issued until January
issue_stock_offering.treatment: Type II - Disclose issuance and use of proceeds.

cpa_exam_tips: Key question: Condition exist at balance sheet date? Yes = Type I (recognize), No = Type II (disclose)
Lawsuit settlement, customer bankruptcy = usually Type I
Stock issuance, acquisitions, casualties = usually Type II
Both types must be evaluated through issuance/available date

key_points: Type I: Condition existed at BS date → Recognize (adjust statements)
Type II: Condition arose after BS date → Disclose only
Evaluate through date financial statements issued/available to be issued
Lawsuit settlements, customer bankruptcy = often Type I. Stock issuance, fire loss = Type II
